email.body1:
Olivia, saw Selerix and Pacific Life launched a digital Evidence of Insurability integration on BenSelect.

More integrations usually mean signals fire faster than ops can route them into action, and good broker and employer accounts go cold in the gap. Our AI SDR turns a signal into a researched, personalized, logged touch with zero rep time: 3-5x more meetings per rep, same team.

I built a personalized signal play for Selerix off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress around 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Olivia, quick follow-up for Selerix.

For a revenue ops and enablement leader, the biggest measurable leak is usually time between a signal firing and a rep acting on it, plus the data hygiene work that eats cycles. Tightening that is where lift hides: our best practices alone tend to raise reply rates 50 to 70 percent.

Worth 15 minutes? I'll walk you through a teardown of your current outbound and three things I'd change to cut that latency.
email.body3:
Olivia, last bit of proof for Selerix.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to 2.7M dollars in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Selerix's reply rate likely compares to other benefits and HR tech companies. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Olivia, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If cutting signal-to-action latency without adding headcount isn't a priority while the Pacific Life integration ramps, no problem at all. Timing is everything right after a launch, and I know that stretch keeps ops busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your ops motion? I'll tailor it to Selerix either way.
